data.name: PcOptimize.Intro
data.value: CrosshairPro never changes system settings — each item below only explains the tweak and links to its management page. Click Open and make the change yourself; adjust one item at a time and measure the result.

data.name: PcOptimize.VendorNotFound
data.value: No NVIDIA/AMD control panel detected. Open it from the Start menu.

data.name: PcOptimize.WinVerNote
data.value: Paths follow Windows 11. For Control Panel items, continue inside the opened window as described.

data.name: PcOptimize.GameModeDesc
data.value: While a game is running, Windows prioritizes resources and pauses update installs and restart notifications for steadier frame rates. Turn on the toggle in the opened Game Mode page; the benefit is bigger on PCs with many background apps or frequent updates.

data.name: PcOptimize.GameBarDesc
data.value: The Game Bar and its widgets are resident overlay processes; disabling them reduces in-game overlay overhead and accidental key presses. Turn off options like "Allow your controller to open Game Bar" in the opened page and re-enable temporarily when recording. Note: keep it if you rely on the Game Bar FPS overlay.

data.name: PcOptimize.BackgroundRecordingDesc
data.value: Background recording keeps writing the last seconds of gameplay to disk and occupies the encoder. In the opened Captures page (Game DVR on Windows 10), turn off "Record what happened" and "Record in the background while playing a game"; shorten "Record the last" if you still want highlights. Biggest benefit on integrated or low-end GPUs.

data.name: PcOptimize.StartupAppsDesc
data.value: Fewer resident background programs free memory and CPU; high-impact startup entries also slow boot and worsen 1% lows. Sort by "Startup impact" in the opened page and disable launchers and updaters you do not need.

data.name: PcOptimize.NotificationsDndDesc
data.value: Notification banners steal focus in games, causing stutters and distractions. Enable Do not disturb in the opened page, then under "Turn on do not disturb automatically" check "When playing a game" and "When using an app in full screen".

data.name: PcOptimize.MemoryIntegrityDesc
data.value: Core isolation (HVCI) validates kernel code via virtualization, which costs measurable performance on older CPUs (pre-Intel 7th gen or pre-Zen 2) — evaluate turning it off for maximum FPS. Toggle "Memory integrity" in the opened Core isolation page, then restart. Note: disabling it weakens kernel exploit protection, and managed PCs may block the change — weigh it yourself.

data.name: PcOptimize.UpdateActiveHoursDesc
data.value: Active hours prevent automatic restarts during your gaming sessions; you can also pause updates before important matches. In the opened page set active hours manually to cover your gaming time, or pause updates as needed.

data.name: PcOptimize.UninstallUnusedAppsDesc
data.value: Uninstalling bundled antivirus, toolbars and other resident software frees disk space and background resources. Sort by size or usage in the opened page and uninstall programs you no longer use.

data.name: PcOptimize.PowerPlanDesc
data.value: Avoids idle downclocking and frequency-ramp latency under burst load. Pick the "High performance" plan in the opened Power Options; on laptops also set the power mode to "Best performance" under Power and battery. Note: watch thermals and battery life on laptops.

data.name: PcOptimize.UsbSelectiveSuspendDesc
data.value: Prevents Windows from suspending idle USB ports, fixing lag or disconnects on mice, keyboards and capture cards. In the opened advanced power settings expand "USB settings > USB selective suspend setting" and set both On battery and Plugged in to Disabled. Note: slightly higher standby power draw.

data.name: PcOptimize.PcieLinkStatePmDesc
data.value: Keeps the PCIe link at full speed, avoiding micro-stutters from GPU link sleep and wake. In the opened advanced power settings set "PCI Express > Link State Power Management" to Off. Note: slightly higher power draw; keep the default on laptops that rely on ASPM for thermals.

data.name: PcOptimize.PowerSleepTimeoutsDesc
data.value: Prevents the screen turning off or the PC going to sleep while you are downloading, spectating or idling in-game. In the opened page extend the Plugged in screen and sleep timeouts or set them to Never.

data.name: PcOptimize.GraphicsHagsDesc
data.value: Lets the GPU manage its own VRAM and task queues for slightly lower latency; DLSS Frame Generation also requires it. Turn on "Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling" in the opened Default graphics settings page, then restart. Note: requires an NVIDIA Pascal or newer GPU with recent drivers; turn it back off if you see glitches.

data.name: PcOptimize.FullscreenOptimizationsDesc
data.value: Windows optimizes fullscreen and borderless games via the flip model; if an older game misbehaves or feels laggy, tune it per game. In the opened Graphics page add the game exe and use "Options" to set GPU preference or disable windowed game optimizations; legacy games can also use exe Properties > Compatibility > "Disable fullscreen optimizations".

data.name: PcOptimize.RefreshRateMaxDesc
data.value: After a fresh install or a cable change Windows often falls back to 60 Hz — set your monitor's maximum refresh rate to get the smoothness and input lag you paid for. Open "Advanced display settings" in the opened page and pick the highest value under "Select a refresh rate".

data.name: PcOptimize.HdrSettingsDesc
data.value: On an HDR display, enabling HDR and Auto HDR greatly improves picture quality; SDR displays do not need it. Turn on "Use HDR" in the opened page and expand the toggle for Auto HDR. Note: laptops disable HDR on battery; competitive players chasing maximum FPS may keep it off. Win+Alt+B toggles HDR quickly.

data.name: PcOptimize.DisplayScalingDesc
data.value: Non-integer scaling blurs the UI and crosshair mapping; competitive players use 100% for pixel-crisp visuals and a consistent pointer speed. Set "Scale" to 100% in the opened Display page and keep the native resolution. Note: text gets small on high-DPI laptops; sign out to apply.

data.name: PcOptimize.VisualEffectsDesc
data.value: Turning off transparency and animations reduces desktop composition overhead — noticeable on older or integrated-GPU machines. Choose "Adjust for best performance" (or a custom set keeping font smoothing) in the opened Performance Options; you can also disable transparency under Settings > Personalization > Colors.

data.name: PcOptimize.NicPowerManagementDesc
data.value: Disabling adapter power saving prevents mid-match drops, latency spikes and disconnects. In the opened Network Connections page right-click the adapter > Properties > Configure: under Power Management uncheck "Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power", and under Advanced disable "Energy Efficient Ethernet" style options. Admin rights are required to change.

data.name: PcOptimize.ProxyVpnDesc
data.value: Proxies and VPNs add routing hops and latency, and online matchmaking may place you on distant servers. Turn off automatic and manual proxy in the opened page; disconnect or remove VPNs. Note: corporate networks may require the proxy — disable it only while gaming.

data.name: PcOptimize.DeliveryOptimizationDesc
data.value: Caps Windows Update background upload and download bandwidth so updates do not spike your ping mid-game. In the opened Delivery Optimization page limit background download and upload bandwidth by percentage or absolute values.

data.name: PcOptimize.StorageSenseDesc
data.value: Automatically cleans temp files and the Recycle Bin, keeping free space on the system drive (especially SSDs) to avoid stutter when it runs full. Turn on Storage Sense in the opened page, set a schedule, or click "Run Storage Sense now".

data.name: PcOptimize.OptimizeDrivesDesc
data.value: Defragmenting HDDs and periodic TRIM for SSDs maintain read and write performance; you can also check drive health here. In the opened Optimize Drives window select a drive and click Analyze or Optimize, and keep weekly scheduled optimization on. Note: SSDs need no manual defrag — Windows runs TRIM automatically (the UI shows "Optimize", not "Defragment", for SSDs).

data.name: PcOptimize.GameInstallSsdDesc
data.value: SSD random reads are far faster than HDDs, greatly cutting load times and open-world texture-streaming stutter (mainly loads, not maximum FPS). In the opened page set "New apps will save to" to an SSD drive; migrate installed games from Steam or your launcher.

data.name: PcOptimize.GpuDriverUpdateDesc
data.value: New drivers often bring performance and stability fixes for new games; a bad driver can also be rolled back here. In Device Manager expand "Display adapters", right-click the GPU and choose "Update driver" (or roll back under Properties > Driver); getting the latest from NVIDIA/AMD/Intel or their apps is recommended.

data.name: PcOptimize.OptionalDriverUpdatesDesc
data.value: Windows Update "Optional updates" ships WHQL-certified chipset and peripheral drivers — more reliable than third-party driver managers. Expand "Driver updates" in the opened page and install what you need.

data.name: PcOptimize.VendorGpuPanelDesc
data.value: The NVIDIA/AMD/Intel control panels expose low-latency mode, V-Sync, per-game profiles and color output — deeper tuning beyond Windows settings. Click Open to auto-detect the installed panel (NVIDIA/AMD); if none is found, open it from the Start menu (NVIDIA App / AMD Adrenalin / Intel graphics software).

data.name: PcOptimize.PointerPrecisionDesc
data.value: "Enhance pointer precision" is mouse acceleration; turning it off makes wrist movement map 1:1 to your view, stabilizing aim muscle memory (a common FPS setting). In the opened Mouse Properties > Pointer Options tab uncheck "Enhance pointer precision" and click OK. If the wrong tab opens, switch to Pointer Options manually.

data.name: PcOptimize.AudioEnhancementsDesc
data.value: Audio enhancement DSP adds processing latency and can cause crackling or conflicts with in-game voice on some drivers. In the opened Sound control panel select the playback device > Properties > Enhancements and check "Disable all enhancements"; on Windows 11 you can also set "Audio enhancements" to Off under Settings > System > Sound. Note: Dolby, loudness equalization and similar effects will be disabled.

data.name: PcOptimize.MythsIntro
data.value: The tweaks below appear in many online "optimization guides" but are placebo or even harmful. CrosshairPro never performs them and we do not recommend trying:

data.name: PcOptimize.Myth.RegistryCleaners
data.value: "Registry cleaners/optimizers": Microsoft officially discourages them — stale entries have near-zero performance impact, and deleting the wrong keys can break apps or even prevent boot.

data.name: PcOptimize.Myth.ServiceDisabling
data.value: "Mass-disabling Windows services": idle services do not consume CPU; FPS gains are near zero while updates, audio or networking often break. Trim startup apps instead.

data.name: PcOptimize.Myth.TimerResolution
data.value: "Forcing 0.5 ms timer resolution": Windows 11 applies timer requests per process, so global hacks mostly no longer work; average FPS barely changes while power draw rises.

data.name: PcOptimize.Myth.RamCleaner
data.value: "RAM cleaners/boosters": free memory is used as file cache — "emptier is faster" is a myth; wiping the standby list forces re-reading from disk and causes stutters.

data.name: PcOptimize.Myth.SsdDefrag
data.value: "Manually defragmenting SSDs": SSDs have no mechanical seek cost — manual defrag only adds wear; Windows already optimizes SSDs via TRIM.

data.name: PcOptimize.Myth.BoosterSuites
data.value: "Game booster suites": tested average-FPS gains are near zero — they mostly kill background processes and clear caches, while running resident in the background themselves.

data.name: Cs2.VideoFileNote
data.value: CrosshairPro only saves to its local config and does not modify video.txt directly. Writes are skipped while the game is running to avoid VAC and Steam cloud-sync conflicts.

data.name: Cs2.AutoexecFileNote
data.value: CrosshairPro only saves to its local config and does not modify autoexec.cfg directly. Configure autoexec loading inside the game.

data.name: Cs2.GenerateConfigDesc
data.value: Generate an exec-able .cfg from the current options to place in the game cfg folder manually; game files are never written directly and only safe whitelisted cvars are included.
